title: Troailt mygeayrt Ellan Vannin
description: Ten short stories about travelling around the Isle of Man: a cyclist on the mountain road, a week on the bus network, a day at a cove, an old church with bats, a letter from a Thai student of Manx, a flood in Laxey, a week on a farm, a night under the stars, a boxing apprentice on the steam train to Port Erin, and an octet on its way to a music festival.
topic: Travelling around the Isle of Man

lessons.title: Y daawheeylleyder er y reeast
lessons.summary: Gervase Coultard, a cyclist from Douglas, takes up his friend's challenge to ride the mountain road from Ramsey to Douglas in under two hours: the wind blows over the silent moor, his left ankle hurts, the wind slowly weakens, an inch of rain lies on the road at the top, and he arrives after an hour and forty minutes.
lessons.text:
Ta Gervase Coultard ny daawheeylleyder. T'eh cummal ayns Doolish, as dagh Jesarn t'eh goll mygeayrt yn ellan myr daawheeylleyder. Ayns y tourey shoh, hug e charrey doolane da: “Gow y raad harrish ny sleityn veih Rhumsaa gys Doolish ayns ny sloo na daa oor.”

She doolane mooar eh. Ta'n raad shen goll seose harrish y reeast, ard eddyr ny sleityn. Cha nel thieyn ny biljyn er y reeast, agh faiyr, clagh as ushtey, as ta'n geay sheidey er dy kinjagh. Va fys ec Gervase dy row eh femoil goaill ushtey as bee marish, er-yn-oyr nagh vel shapp erbee er y reeast.

Er moghrey Jesarn, hie Gervase gys Rhumsaa er y traen. Va daawheeylleyderyn elley ec y stashoon, as v'ad goll gys y reeast neesht.

“Vel oo goll harrish ny sleityn jiu?” dooyrt ben aeg rish.

“Ta,” dooyrt Gervase. “Agh ta'n geay sheidey veih'n jiass. Bare lhiam geay veih'n twoaie.”

Ghow eh toshiaght. Va'n raad goll seose, as seose, as seose. Lurg lieh oor, va pian ayns e abane chiare. Hass eh son tammylt, as ren eh jeeaghyn er e abane. Cha row eh brisht, agh va'n abane gortit beggan.

Va'n geay sheidey ny smoo as ny smoo, as v'eh goll dy moal. Agh ec y traa cheddin, va'n reeast aalin. Va'n reeast tostagh: cha row sheean erbee ayn, agh y geay as ushag ny ghaa. Va Gervase tostagh neesht, son cha row fer erbee echey dy loayrt rish.

Lurg tammylt, ren y geay lhaggee. V'eh lhaggee beggan as beggan, as ec y jerrey, cha row eh sheidey veg. Va Gervase abyl goll ny s'tappee reesht.

Ec mullagh y raad, haink fliaghey trome. Ayns minnid ny ghaa, va oarlagh dy ushtey er y raad, as ayns boayl ny ghaa, daa oarlagh. Ren Gervase goll dy meein, son va'n raad fliugh.

Haink eh gys Doolish lurg oor as daeed minnid. Va'n carrey echey shassoo ec y dorrys.

“Ren oo eh!” dooyrt y carrey.

“Ren,” dooyrt Gervase. “Agh ta my abane gortit, as cha jean mee doolane elley derrey'n mee noa.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n doolane hug y carrey da Gervase?
Hug eh doolane da goll harrish ny sleityn veih Rhumsaa gys Doolish ayns ny sloo na daa oor.
Cre'n fa va eh femoil goaill bee as ushtey?
Er-yn-oyr nagh vel shapp erbee er y reeast.
Cre'n geay bare lesh Gervase?
Bare lesh Gervase geay veih'n twoaie.
Cre haink er abane Gervase?
Va pian ayns e abane chiare, as v'eh gortit beggan.
Cre ren y geay lurg tammylt?
Ren y geay lhaggee, derrey nagh row eh sheidey veg.

lessons.title: Y greasane barrooseyn
lessons.summary: Loveday Rendell from England spends a week on the island without a car and uses the bus network: paying once for the whole week is advantageous, Sunday is unfavourable with few buses, the windows are dirty, the bus passes roadworks with cones on the opposite side of the road, and in Port Erin a chance meeting with her old schoolfriend Anselm Lockwood ends her bus trips.
lessons.text:
Haink Loveday Rendell veih Sostyn gys Ellan Vannin son shiaghtin. Cha row gleashtan eck, as cha row ee laccal fer y ghoaill. “Ta greasane barrooseyn mie ayns Ellan Vannin,” dooyrt ee rish hene. “Hem mygeayrt yn ellan er y varroose.”

Er y chied voghrey, hie ee gys stashoon ny barrooseyn ayns Doolish. Va ben ec y oik. Hug ee lioar veg da Loveday lesh caslys jeh'n ghreasane: ny raaidyn, ny stashoonyn, as ny traaghyn.

“Foddee oo eeck un cheayrt son y clane shiaghtin,” dooyrt y ven. “Ta shen vondeishagh da sleih ta goll er y varroose dagh laa. T'eh ny sloo deyr na eeck reesht dagh moghrey.”

“As Jedoonee?” dooyrt Loveday.

“Ta Jedoonee neuvondeishagh,” dooyrt y ven. “Cha nel feddynaght vooar ec ny barrooseyn Jedoonee. Ta barroose dagh oor ayn, as cha nel barroose erbee lurg shey er y clag 'syn astyr.”

Ren Loveday eeck son y clane shiaghtin. Er y Jerdein, hie ee er y varroose gys Purt ny h-Inshey. Va'n barroose lane, as va uinnagyn y varroose sallagh: v'ad sallagh lesh fliaghey as joan. Cha row Loveday abyl fakin y cheayn trooid ny uinnagyn sallagh.

Faggys da Balley Chashtal, va obbyr er y raad. Va cughlinyn jiarg as bane er y raad, as dooinney ny hassoo eddyr ny cughlinyn. Ren y barroose goll er y çheu condaigagh jeh'n raad, dy meein. Va gleashtanyn çheet er y çheu condaigagh, as hass y barroose derrey v'ad er goll shaghey. Eisht hie eh er y raad hoshiaght reesht.

Ren Loveday smooinaght dy beagh y jurnaa liauyr er coontey yn obbyr. Agh va'n jurnaa giare, contraartagh da shen v'ee smooinaght.

Ayns Purt ny h-Inshey, haink dooinney shenn er y varroose. Ren eh jeeaghyn er Loveday, as eisht ren eh gearey.

“Loveday? Loveday Rendell?” dooyrt eh. She Anselm Lockwood v'ayn. Va Anselm as Loveday ayns y scoill cheddin ayns Sostyn, roish daeed blein.

“Anselm! Cre t'ou jannoo ayns shoh?” dooyrt Loveday.

“Ta mee cummal ayns shoh,” dooyrt Anselm. “Haink mee gys Ellan Vannin roish feed blein.”

She quail taghyrtagh v'ayn. Cha row Loveday ny Anselm jerkal rish. Agh va'n quail taghyrtagh shen y red share jeh'n turrys. Jedoonee, cha row feme ec Loveday er y varroose erbee: ghow Anselm ee mygeayrt yn ellan ayns e ghleashtan.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa hie Loveday mygeayrt yn ellan er y varroose?
Cha row gleashtan eck, as ta greasane barrooseyn mie ayns Ellan Vannin.
Cre'n fa va eeck son y clane shiaghtin vondeishagh?
Va shen ny sloo deyr na eeck reesht dagh moghrey.
Cre'n fa va Jedoonee neuvondeishagh?
Cha nel feddynaght vooar ec ny barrooseyn Jedoonee.
Cre va er y raad faggys da Balley Chashtal?
Va cughlinyn jiarg as bane er y raad, as dooinney eddyr ny cughlinyn.
Row'n jurnaa liauyr?
Cha row. Contraartagh da shen v'ee smooinaght, va'n jurnaa giare.
Quoi haink er y varroose ayns Purt ny h-Inshey?
Haink Anselm Lockwood er y varroose: va eh ayns y scoill cheddin as Loveday.

lessons.title: Laa ec y chooan
lessons.summary: Damaris Mabey takes her eight-year-old son Rollo to a quiet cove in the south: they find a crab and sea snails in the rock pools, watch gannets diving in the bay, where they come in the mating season, and meet a diver whose finned shoes help him swim under the water.
lessons.text:
Ta Damaris Mabey cummal ayns Doolish marish e mac Rollo, as t'eh hoght bleeaney d'eash. Ayns Mee ny Boaldyn, ghow ad y barroose gys y jiass jeh'n ellan, as hie ad sheese raad beg gys cooan beg ry-hoi'n cheayn. Cha row sleih elley 'sy chooan, agh ny ushagyn.

Ec y cooan, va claghyn mooarey as loghanyn beggey eddyr ny claghyn. Ta'n faarkey goll magh daa cheayrt dagh laa, as tra t'eh goll magh, ta ushtey-marrey faagit ayns ny loghanyn.

“Jeeagh!” dooyrt Rollo. “Ta partan 'sy loghan!”

Va partan beg jiarg fo clagh 'sy loghan. Ren Damaris y partan y hroggal dy meein. “Jeeagh er ny cassyn echey,” dooyrt ee. “Ta hoght cassyn ec partan, as daa laue vooar.” Hug ad y partan reesht 'sy loghan. Ayns loghan elley, va crammagyn beggey doo er ny claghyn. Va dagh crammag goll dy feer moal harrish y clagh.

“Vel crammagyn ayns y faarkey?” dooyrt Rollo.

“Ta,” dooyrt Damaris. “Ta crammagyn faarkey ayn, as crammagyn er y thalloo. Ta'n crammag shoh beaghey ayns y loghan.”

Eisht, ren Damaris soilshaghey da Rollo ny ushagyn harrish y ghullad. Va ny ushagyn mooar as bane, lesh skianyn liauyr. “Shen gantyn,” dooyrt ee. “Ta'n gant tuittym veih'n aer stiagh 'sy cheayn dy ghoaill eeast. Ta ny gantyn çheet dys y ghullad shoh ayns imbagh y cholleeys. Ayns y traa shen, ta'n gant firrinagh as y gant bwoirrinagh shassoo ry-cheilley as cur ny skianyn mygeayrt. She shen y colleeys oc. Lurg y cholleeys, bee oohyn oc.”

Ren Rollo jeeaghyn er y ghullad son tammylt foddey. Eisht honnick eh red doo 'syn ushtey. Va dooinney çheet magh ass y cheayn: thummeyder v'ayn, ayns eaddagh doo. Va braagyn skianagh er e chassyn, myr skianyn eeast.

“Cre'n fa ta ny braagyn shen skianagh?” dooyrt Rollo rish y thummeyder.

“Ta ny braagyn skianagh jannoo eh aashagh dou snaue fo'n ushtey,” dooyrt y thummeyder. “Ta mee thummey ayns y ghullad dagh shiaghtin. Fo'n ushtey, ta ram partanyn ayn, as eeastyn, as crammagyn mooarey.”

Hie Damaris as Rollo dys y thie 'syn astyr. Ayns y barroose, ren Rollo caslys jeh gant, partan as thummeyder.

Feyshtyn:
Cre va eddyr ny claghyn ec y cooan?
Va loghanyn beggey eddyr ny claghyn.
Cre honnick Rollo 'sy chied loghan?
Honnick eh partan beg jiarg fo clagh.
Cre'n traa ta ny gantyn çheet dys y ghullad?
T'ad çheet ayns imbagh y cholleeys.
Quoi haink magh ass y cheayn?
Haink thummeyder magh, ayns eaddagh doo.
Cre'n fa va ny braagyn echey skianagh?
Ta ny braagyn skianagh jannoo eh aashagh da'n thummeyder snaue fo'n ushtey.

lessons.title: Ny craitnagyn 'sy cheeill
lessons.summary: Melisande Arbuthnot, who loves old churches, visits an ivy-covered church in the north: the deacon Eustace Hollins tells her the bishop consecrated it in 1835, shows her a window with biblical pictures and the scroll of the consecration, introduces the respected old organist, and explains the bats in the tower, which people are now more aware of.
lessons.text:
S'mie lesh Melisande Arbuthnot dy chooilley cheeill shenn. Dagh blein, t'ee çheet gys Ellan Vannin son shiaghtin, as t'ee goll mygeayrt yn ellan dy akin keeill shenn ny ghaa. Ayns y vlein shoh, hie ee gys keeill veg ayns y twoaie, faggys da'n cheayn.

Va hibbin harrish boallaghyn y cheeill. Va'n hibbin glass as çhiu, as v'eh goll seose derrey'n mullagh. Ec y dorrys, va dooinney ny hassoo: Eustace Hollins, y jaghin. Ta'n jaghin gobbraghey marish y saggyrt, as t'eh freayll arrey er y cheeill.

“Failt ort,” dooyrt y jaghin. “Va'n cheeill shoh troggit 'sy vlein 1835. Ren yn aspick y cheeill y chasherickey 'sy vlein cheddin. Tra ta keeill noa troggit, ta feme er yn aspick ee y chasherickey roish my vod sleih goll stiagh ayn son shirveish.”

Ren y jaghin soilshaghey uinnag vooar da Melisande. Va jallooyn bibleagh 'syn uinnag: Noah as y lhong echey, Moses 'sy cheayn, as Yeesey marish ny eeasteyryn. “Ta ny jallooyn bibleagh shoh veih'n vlein 1900,” dooyrt eh.

Eisht, ghow eh scrolley ass kishtey. Va'n scrolley liauyr as bwee. “She scrolley y chasherickey eh shoh,” dooyrt y jaghin. “Ta ennym yn aspick screeuit er y scrolley, as enmyn ny sleih va ayns y cheeill er y laa shen.”

Va kiaull ayns y cheeill. Va organeyr shenn cloie er yn organe. “Shen yn organeyr ain,” dooyrt y jaghin. “T'eh kiare feed blein d'eash, as t'eh cloie ayns y cheeill shoh son tree feed blein. T'eh ammyssit 'sy skeerey slane. Ta ammys ec dy chooilley pheiagh er. She organeyr ammyssit eh.”

“As cre ta ayns y toor?” dooyrt Melisande. Va sheeanyn beggey çheet veih'n toor.

“Craitnagyn,” dooyrt y jaghin. “Ta craitnagyn beayn ayns y toor. 'Sy tourey, ta keead craitnag ayn. T'ad cadley 'sy laa, as t'ad goll magh 'syn oie dy ghoaill beishteigyn. Ta'n craitnag feer veg: cha nel ee ny smoo na laue paitçhey.”

“Vel ny craitnagyn olk son y cheeill?” dooyrt Melisande.

“Va sleih smooinaght shen,” dooyrt y jaghin. “Agh nish, ta tastid ny sleih er ny craitnagyn ny smoo. Ta tastid ain dy vel ny craitnagyn feer scanshoil. Cha nel shin cur soilshey erbee er y toor 'syn oie, myr nagh bee aggle er ny craitnagyn.”

Haink Melisande magh 'syn astyr. Va ny craitnagyn etlagh mygeayrt y toor, harrish yn hibbin.

Feyshtyn:
Cre va harrish boallaghyn y cheeill?
Va hibbin glass harrish ny boallaghyn.
Quoi ren y cheeill y chasherickey?
Ren yn aspick y cheeill y chasherickey 'sy vlein 1835.
Cre va 'syn uinnag vooar?
Va jallooyn bibleagh 'syn uinnag.
Cre va screeuit er y scrolley?
Va ennym yn aspick as enmyn ny sleih screeuit er y scrolley.
Cre'n fa ta'n organeyr ammyssit?
T'eh cloie ayns y cheeill son tree feed blein.
Cre ta ny craitnagyn jannoo 'syn oie?
T'ad goll magh dy ghoaill beishteigyn.

lessons.title: Lettyr veih ynseydagh Thai
lessons.summary: In a letter in Manx to her online teacher Perpetua, the Thai student Kanya writes about travelling round the island: the cold weather far from the equator, the Manx encyclopedia online, the velar sounds and the tap of both languages, a question about her surname, and the warm character of the people she meets.
lessons.text:
Doolish, 14 Mee Souree

Perpetua veen,

Ta mee nish ayns Ellan Vannin son shiaghtin, as ta mee screeu yn lettyr shoh ayns Gaelg, myr dooyrt mee rhyt. T'ou er ve ny ynseyder mie dou: ta mee ny ynseydagh ayd son daa vlein er yn eddyr-voggyl, as ta ynseydee elley ayd ayns Nalbin as ayns Sostyn. Nish ta mee jurnaaghey mygeayrt yn ellan dy loayrt Gaelg rish ny sleih.

Ta mee er ve jurnaaghey er y traen, er y varroose as er my chassyn. Ta'n emshir feer feayr! Ayns Bangkok, ta'n emshir çheh dy kinjagh, son ta'n Çheer Thai ny sniessey da'n meanchiarkyl na Ellan Vannin. Faggys da'n meanchiarkyl, ta'n ghrian ard 'sy speyr 'sy vlein slane.

Va mee lhaih mychione Ellan Vannin hoshiaght 'sy kicklipaid ayns Gaelg er yn eddyr-voggyl. Ta ny smoo na queig thousane art 'sy kicklipaid shen. Va mee goaill yindys dy vel kicklipaid ayns çhengey cho beg.

Ta mee ronsaghey fockley ny çhengaghyn ec yn ollooscoill ayns Bangkok, as ta mee clashtyn dy vel Gaelg as Thaish cosoyllagh ayns aght ny ghaa. Ta sheeanyn coghooysagh ayns Gaelg, myr y sheean ayns mean ‘moghrey’: ta'n sheean shoh jeant ec cooyl y veeal. Ta sheeanyn coghooysagh ayns Thaish neesht, agh cha nel y sheean cheddin ain. As ta'n sheean ayns mean ‘mooarane’ ny crank: ta'n çhengey bwoalley y veeal un cheayrt, dy tappee. Ta crank ayns Thaish myrgeddin. Myr shen, ta'n crank ayns Gaelg cosoyllagh rish y crank ain.

Ren dooinney ayns Rhumsaa feysht orrym: “Cre'n sliennoo t'ayd?” Dinsh mee da dy vel sliennoo ec dy chooilley pheiagh 'sy Çheer Thai, agh dy vel sleih gra yn chied ennym ny smoo na'n sliennoo, as nagh row sliennooyn ec sleih 'sy Çheer Thai roish y vlein 1913. Va eh goaill yindys.

Ta ambee mie ec ny sleih ayns shoh. T'ad çheh as dooie, as t'ad loayrt dy meein, ga dy vel my Ghaelg feer lag ny keayrtyn. Ta'n ambee shen cosoyllagh rish ambee ny sleih 'sy Çheer Thai.

Jeheiney, hem jurnaaghey dys Purt ny h-Inshey. Bee lettyr elley ayd dy gerrid.

Lesh graih,
Kanya

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta Kanya?
She ynseydagh Thai ee: t'ee ynsaghey Gaelg rish Perpetua er yn eddyr-voggyl.
Cre'n fa ta'n emshir çheh ayns Bangkok?
Son ta'n Çheer Thai ny sniessey da'n meanchiarkyl.
Raad va Kanya lhaih mychione Ellan Vannin hoshiaght?
Va ee lhaih 'sy kicklipaid ayns Gaelg er yn eddyr-voggyl.
Cre ta cosoyllagh ayns Gaelg as Thaish?
Ta sheeanyn coghooysagh ayns yn daa hengey, as ta crank ayns yn daa hengey.
Cre'n ambee t'ec ny sleih ayns Ellan Vannin?
T'ad çheh as dooie.

lessons.title: Yn thooilley ayns Laksaa
lessons.summary: Thurstan Crosland, a retired engineer, takes the electric railway to Laxey to visit his daughter Sidony just as the river floods her neighbourhood: a neighbour's generator powers a machine, a long pipe takes the water out, soldiers and civilians help, the government gives money for support, a board that governs the rivers plans new housing, and the village slowly recovers.
lessons.text:
Ta Thurstan Crosland ny shenn jeshaghteyr ass Doolish. Ta'n inneen echey, Sidony, cummal ayns Laksaa, ayns thie beg faggys da'n awin. Ayns Mee Houney, ghow Thurstan y raad-yiarn lectragh gys Laksaa dy akin ee.

Va fliaghey trome ayn son daa laa as daa oie. 'Sy voghrey, haink yn awin harrish y broogh. Va thooilley ayns y nabooys slane faggys da'n awin. Va'n ushtey ayns ny straiddyn, as stiagh 'sy thieyn. Ayns thie Sidony, va'n ushtey jeih oarleeyn er yrjid er y laare.

Cha row lectraghys erbee ayns y nabooys. Agh va gienneyder ec naboo Sidony, as hug eh y gienneyder ayns y traid. Ren y gienneyder lectraghys son soilshey as son greie va tayrn ushtey magh ass ny thieyn. Hug Thurstan pioban liauyr veih'n ghreie gys y traid. Va'n ushtey goll trooid y phioban, magh ass y thie, as sheese dys yn awin reesht.

Haink sidooryn as sleih shivoilagh dy obbraghey marish ny naboonyn. Va ny sleih shivoilagh veih'n valley hene, as veih Doolish. V'ad cur bee as eaddagh çhirrym da ny sleih ayns y nabooys. Va thie ny skeerey foshlit, as va sleih cadley ayn.

Lurg tree laaghyn, va'n thooilley ersooyl. Agh va ny thieyn fliugh as sallagh. Ren y Reiltys argid y chur son pohlldal ny sleih. “Ta'n pohlldal shoh feer vie,” dooyrt Sidony. “Agh ta feme ain er ny smoo na argid. Ta feme ain er thieys noa, ayns boayl ard.”

Ayns y Tinvaal, va sleih loayrt mychione thieys. Ta bing ayn ta gurneil ny awinyn as y thalloo mygeayrt orroo. Dooyrt y bing dy jinnagh eh boalley ard y hroggal ry-hoi'n awin, as dy beagh thieys noa troggit er y chronk ny s'yrjey. “Ta feme ain er gurneil ny awinyn ny share,” dooyrt fer jeh'n bing. “Ta'n emshir caghlaa, as bee thooilley elley ayn.”

Ren y nabooys slaanee beggan as beggan. Ren ny naboonyn gobbraghey ry-cheilley dy ghlenney ny thieyn. Ayns tree meeghyn, va thie Sidony çhirrym reesht. Ren Laksaa slaanee veih'n thooilley, as va pohlldal ny naboonyn ny smoo na pohlldal erbee elley.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa va thooilley ayns y nabooys?
Va fliaghey trome ayn son daa laa, as haink yn awin harrish y broogh.
Cre ren y gienneyder?
Ren y gienneyder lectraghys son soilshey as son greie va tayrn ushtey magh ass ny thieyn.
Cre hug Thurstan veih'n ghreie gys y traid?
Hug eh pioban liauyr veih'n ghreie gys y traid.
Quoi haink dy obbraghey marish ny naboonyn?
Haink sidooryn as sleih shivoilagh.
Cre ta'n bing ayns y Tinvaal gurneil?
T'eh gurneil ny awinyn as y thalloo mygeayrt orroo.
Ren Laksaa slaanee veih'n thooilley?
Ren. Ren y nabooys slaanee beggan as beggan, as ayns tree meeghyn va thie Sidony çhirrym reesht.

lessons.title: Shiaghtin er y thie-ollee
lessons.summary: Ten-year-old Kester from England spends a week on Millicent Yeoman's farm near Sulby: he pulls and washes onions, picks beans, counts a dozen eggs, pushes down an old cheese press, sees a pregnant cow, and learns about the bleaching field where women once laid linen in the sun.
lessons.text:
Haink Kester, guilley jeih bleeaney d'eash, veih Sostyn marish e voir son shiaghtin er thie-ollee faggys da Sulby. She Millicent Yeoman ben y thie-ollee. Ta ollagh, kirree as kiarkyn eck, as garey mooar lane lus.

Er y chied voghrey, hie Kester magh 'sy gharey marish Millicent. Va unnish as praaseyn 'sy thalloo, as poanraghyn er ny lussyn ard. Ren Kester dagh unnish y hayrn ass y thalloo. Va dagh unnish mooar as bane, agh va thalloo er.

“Ta feme ain er oonlaghey yn unnish,” dooyrt Millicent. Hug ee kishtey lane unnish ayns ushtey. “Oonlee dagh unnish dy mie,” dooyrt ee. Ren Kester oonlaghey dagh unnish, derrey nagh row thalloo erbee orroo.

Eisht, ren ad ny poanraghyn y ghoaill. Va ny poanraghyn glass as liauyr. “Bee shin gee poanraghyn as unnish son shibbyr jiu,” dooyrt Millicent.

Lurg shen, hie ad gys thie ny kiarkyn. “Ta feme aym er dussan ooh,” dooyrt Millicent. “Jean coontey ad: dussan, shen daa ooh jeig.” Hooar Kester dussan ooh, as hooar eh daa ooh elley. “Dussan as daa,” dooyrt eh.

'Sy thie-bainney, va greie mooar shenn jeant jeh fuygh as yiarn. “She faastan caashey eh shoh,” dooyrt Millicent. “Ta shin cur y caashey noa ayns y faastan, as ta'n faastan cur yn ushtey magh ass y chaashey. Lurg mee ny ghaa, bee caashey mie ain.” Hug Kester ooilley e niart er y faastan. V'eh trome, agh va'n faastan goll sheese dy meein.

'Sy vagher, va booa vooar ny lhie er y faiyr. “Ta'n booa shoh torragh,” dooyrt Millicent. “Bee booa veg eck ayns jeih laa. Ta booa torragh trome as moal.” Ren Kester jeeaghyn er y vooa son tammylt.

Va magher beg ec cooyl y thie. “She magher giallaghey v'ayn shoh,” dooyrt Millicent. “Roish keead blein, va ny mraane cur lieen er y faiyr 'sy ghrian. Va'n ghrian jannoo yn lieen bane. She giallaghey va sleih gra rish shen.”

Er y laa s'jerree, ren Kester gee caashey veih'n faastan, lesh arran as unnish. “Shoh y caashey share 'sy theihll,” dooyrt eh.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ren Kester lesh yn unnish?
Ren eh dagh unnish y hayrn ass y thalloo, as ren eh oonlaghey ad.
Cre'n earroo dy oohyn ta ayns dussan?
Ta daa ooh jeig ayns dussan.
Cre ta'n faastan jannoo?
Ta'n faastan cur yn ushtey magh ass y chaashey.
Cre'n fa ta'n booa trome?
Ta'n booa torragh, as bee booa veg eck ayns jeih laa.
Cre va'n giallaghey?
Va ny mraane cur lieen er y faiyr 'sy ghrian, as va'n ghrian jannoo yn lieen bane.

lessons.title: Oie fo ny rollageyn
lessons.summary: Petronella Rennick takes nine-year-old Crispian Dimmock and his father to a dark place in the south on a freezing night at zero degrees: she talks of a hundred billion stars, extraterrestrial life and the asteroids, shows a stone from the sky with calcium and sulphur in it, explains the protons in the sun, and they cut paper stars with templates.
lessons.text:
Ta Petronella Rennick ronsaghey ny rollageyn. Ayns y gheurey, t'ee goaill sleih gys boayl dorraghey ayns jiass yn ellan, faggys da'n cheayn. Cha nel soilshey erbee ayns shen, as myr shen ta ny rollageyn ry-akin dy mie. Ayns Mee Ouyr, haink guilley ennym Crispian Dimmock, as eh nuy bleeaney d'eash, marish e yishag.

Va'n oie feer feayr. Va'n çhiassid neunhee: neunhee keimyn. “Neunhee!” dooyrt Crispian. “Ta'n ushtey goll ny rio nish.”

Ren Petronella soilshaghey ny rollageyn da Crispian. “Ta ny smoo na keead villoon rollage ayns y possan rollageyn ain,” dooyrt ee. “As ta ram possanyn elley ayns y seihll.”

“Keead villoon?” dooyrt Crispian. “Vel bea neuhallooinagh ayn, eisht?”

“Cha nel fys ain,” dooyrt Petronella. “Cha nel shin er fakin bea neuhallooinagh rieau. Ta sleih screeu lioaryn mychione sleih neuhallooinagh, agh cha nel ad ayn agh 'sy smooinaght oc. Agh ta ram planaidyn ayn, as foddee dy vel bea er planaid ny ghaa.”

Eisht, loayr ee mychione ny roltagee. “Ta roltagee goll mygeayrt y ghrian, myr ny planaidyn,” dooyrt ee. “Agh t'ad beg, as cha nel ad cruinn. Ta'n chooid smoo jeu eddyr y planaid jiarg as Jupiter.” Ghow ee clagh veg ass kishtey. “Haink y clagh shoh veih'n speyr. Va'n clagh shoh ayrn jeh fer jeh ny roltagee. Ta kelkium as sulfur ayn. Ta kelkium ayns ny craueyn ain neesht, as ayns bainney.”

Ren Crispian y clagh y hroggal gys e stroin. “Ta soar olk eck,” dooyrt eh.

“Shen y sulfur,” dooyrt Petronella, gearey. “Ta soar oohyn brisht ec sulfur.”

“As cre ta'n ghrian?” dooyrt e yishag.

“Ta'n ghrian lane dy phrotaneyn,” dooyrt Petronella. “Ta protane beg, beg: cha vod oo protane y akin. Ayns cree ny greiney, ta ny protaneyn bwoalley ry-cheilley, as ta shen cur soilshey as çhiass dooin.”

Ec y jerrey, hie ad stiagh ayns thie beg çheh. Va pabyr as clowanyn er y voayrd. Ren Crispian rollage y yannoo lesh clowan: hug eh y clowan er y phabyr, as ren eh giarrey mygeayrt y chlowan. Ren e yishag roltagee y yannoo lesh clowan elley. Hug ad ny rollageyn pabyr er y voalley ayns thie Crispian.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa ta ny rollageyn ry-akin dy mie ayns y boayl shoh?
Cha nel soilshey erbee ayns shen.
Cre va'n çhiassid?
Va'n çhiassid neunhee keimyn.
Cre'n earroo dy rollageyn ta 'sy possan ain?
Ta ny smoo na keead villoon rollage ayn.
Cre ta ayns y clagh veih'n speyr?
Ta kelkium as sulfur ayn.
Cre ren Crispian lesh y clowan?
Hug eh y clowan er y phabyr, as ren eh giarrey mygeayrt y chlowan.

lessons.title: Y doarneyr ayns Purt Çhiarn
lessons.summary: Nineteen-year-old Osbert Trelawny takes the steam train each day from Douglas to Port Erin for his apprenticeship at a boxing club, a venture of the old boxer Wolfram Strasser and his partner Jocasta Upshaw, an archer; Wolfram tells him how his Prussian grandfather fled the dictator in 1936, was an outcast in London and found a home in boxing.
lessons.text:
Ta Osbert Trelawny nuy bleeaney jeig d'eash, as t'eh cummal ayns Doolish. Dagh moghrey, t'eh goaill y traen-gaal veih Doolish gys Purt Çhiarn. Ta'n jurnaa goll ny smoo na lieh oor, as t'eh lhaih lioar er y traen.

Ayns Purt Çhiarn, ta Osbert jannoo prindeysaght ayns thie doarneyrys. T'eh ynsaghey dy ve ny ynseyder doarneyrys. She Wolfram Strasser fer y thie. Va Wolfram ny doarneyr ayns e aegid, as nish t'eh tree feed as jeih blein d'eash. Ta'n prindeysaght goll son daa vlein.

Ta'n thie doarneyrys ny ventyr: ventyr ec Wolfram as ec y parteeas echey, Jocasta Upshaw. She sideyr ee, as t'ee ynsaghey paitçhyn dy ve ny sideyr. Ta'n daa obbyr ayns y thie cheddin: doarneyrys 'sy voghrey, as y sideyr marish ny paitçhyn eck 'syn astyr. Ta Wolfram as Jocasta ayns parteeas son jeih bleeaney, as ta'n ventyr oc mie.

Er laa fliugh, cha row sleih elley 'sy thie. Ren Osbert feysht er Wolfram: “Cre'n fa haink oo gys doarneyrys?”

“Va my shenn-ayr ny doarneyr,” dooyrt Wolfram. “Va Friedrich yn ennym echey. V'eh prooshagh: v'eh ruggit ayns Berlin, 'sy chooid prooshagh jeh'n Ghermaan. 'Sy vlein 1936, va jaghteyr reill 'sy Ghermaan. Cha row y jaghteyr laccal sleih myr Friedrich. Myr shen, ren Friedrich çhea. Haink yn çhea echey trooid yn Rank, as eisht er lhong gys Sostyn.”

“As cre haink er ayns Sostyn?”

“Ayns Lunnin, v'eh ny vooidjeen. Cha row sleih laccal bentyn rish dooinney prooshagh, as cha row Baarle echey. Agh va thie doarneyrys faggys da'n thie echey. Hie eh stiagh, as ren eh doarneyrys. Va ny sleih ayns y thie doarneyrys dooie rish. Cha row eh ny vooidjeen ayns y thie shen.”

“As v'eh ny doarneyr mie?” dooyrt Osbert.

“Va. Ren eh cosney ram cloieyn,” dooyrt Wolfram. “Dooyrt eh dou: ‘Veih'n jaghteyr, ren mee çhea. Ayns doarneyrys, cha jean mee çhea rieau.’”

Ren Osbert smooinaght er shen er y traen dys y thie 'syn astyr.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Osbert jannoo ayns Purt Çhiarn?
T'eh jannoo prindeysaght ayns thie doarneyrys.
Quoi ta'n parteeas ec Wolfram?
She Jocasta Upshaw y parteeas echey, as she sideyr ee.
Cre'n fa ren Friedrich çhea?
Va jaghteyr reill 'sy Ghermaan, as cha row y jaghteyr laccal sleih myr Friedrich.
Cre'n fa va Friedrich ny vooidjeen ayns Lunnin?
Cha row sleih laccal bentyn rish dooinney prooshagh, as cha row Baarle echey.
Cre ren Friedrich ayns y thie doarneyrys?
Ren eh doarneyrys, as ren eh cosney ram cloieyn.

lessons.title: Yn oghtread er y raad
lessons.summary: Celestine Thornbury leads an octet travelling to a music festival in Ramsey; Lazarus Tunstall polishes his glossy silver horn every morning, they stop to play at the bishop's old residence, sing a bardic song about Patrick driving the snakes off the island, and win a prize.
lessons.text:
Ta Celestine Thornbury stiurey oghtread: possan dy hoght kiaulleyderyn. Ta ny hoght oc cloie kiaull shenn ny h-ellan as goaill arraneyn. Ayns Mee Averil, ghow yn oghtread barroose beg veih Doolish dys y twoaie, dy chloie ec cruinnaght kiaull ayns Rhumsaa.

She Lazarus Tunstall y fer smoo shinney 'syn oghtread. T'eh cloie y cayrn. Ta'n cayrn echey argidagh, as t'eh feer gloasagh. Dagh moghrey, t'eh glenney yn cayrn derrey t'eh gloasagh as gial.

“Cre'n fa t'ou glenney yn cayrn cho mennick?” dooyrt Celestine.

“Va'n cayrn argidagh shoh ec my yishag,” dooyrt Lazarus. “As roish shen, ec e yishag. Lhisagh cayrn argidagh ve gloasagh dy kinjagh.”

Er y raad, hass yn oghtread ec aarys shenn faggys da'n cheayn. Va'n aarys shoh aarys yn aspick son ymmodee cheead blein. Nish, ta sleih elley cummal ayns yn aarys, agh t'ad laccal kiaull. Ren yn oghtread cloie ayns y shamyr vooar ayns yn aarys.

Ren ad arrane bardagh y ghoaill. Ta'n arrane bardagh shoh feer shenn: va bard screeu eh roish ymmodee cheead blein. Ta'n arrane bardagh ginsh skeeal Pherick, y fer casherick. Rere'n skeeal, haink Pherick dys Ellan Vannin, as va aarnieu ayns dagh magher as ayns dagh keyll. Ren Pherick ny ardnieughyn y imman ersooyl, as ny lurg shen, cha row aarnieu erbee ayns Ellan Vannin.

“Vel shen firrinagh?” dooyrt ben aeg tra va'n kiaull harrish.

“Cha nel aarnieu erbee ayns Ellan Vannin jiu,” dooyrt Celestine. “Agh cha nel fys ain dy row aarnieu erbee ayn roish Pherick.”

Eisht, ren Lazarus cloie arrane er y cayrn echey, er e lomarcan. Va sheean y chayrn ard as aalin ayns y shamyr. Va'n cayrn argidagh gloasagh fo'n soilshey.

Ayns Rhumsaa, hooar yn oghtread aundyr ec y chruinnaght. “Va'n arrane bardagh mie,” dooyrt Celestine rish Lazarus. “Agh va'n cayrn echeysyn ny share.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta oghtread?
She possan dy hoght kiaulleyderyn eh.
Cre'n fa ta Lazarus glenney yn cayrn cho mennick?
Va'n cayrn argidagh ec e yishag, as lhisagh eh ve gloasagh dy kinjagh.
C'raad hass yn oghtread er y raad?
Hass ad ec aarys shenn faggys da'n cheayn: aarys yn aspick.
Cre'n skeeal ta'n arrane bardagh ginsh?
T'eh ginsh skeeal Pherick as ny ardnieughyn.
Vel aarnieu erbee ayns Ellan Vannin jiu?
Cha nel aarnieu erbee ayns Ellan Vannin jiu.
